statements.statement: FY27 proposed level-services school budget stands at $28,259,974, about $2 million more than the FY26 budget.
Health insurance is rising from 14% to 16% of the school budget, an increase estimated at $800,000-$900,000.
Salaries and expenses are both rising about $1 million, driven by contractual increases (teachers, paraprofessional union, custodians).

statements.amount_as_heard: from about $1.3 million to about $2.7 million
statements.statement: Town manager cited town-wide health insurance cost roughly doubling, from about $1.3 million last year to about $2.7 million.
Combined general and special education student transportation costs are up about $300,000 from last year, attributed to a sole bidder (D-Bus) with no competing offers.
Based on current revenue projections, a reduction of about $1.7 million was cited as a possible scenario, described as 'a third option which is not a good option.'

statements.amount_as_heard: another $1.6-1.7 million, making a $3.7 million increase over FY26
statements.statement: Committee directed the business administrator to prepare a 'strategic investment' budget adding about $1.7 million to level services, for a total increase of about $3.7 million over FY26 (before any town revenue offset).
The town manager's earlier estimate gave the schools about $86,000 in new revenue; described as including the $900,000 health insurance increase but not town employee COLA increases.

statements.amount_as_heard: $1.3 million initial revenue projection; schools' 53.3% share would be $696,521.74
statements.statement: Initial town revenue projection cited at $1.3 million, of which the schools' traditional 53.3% share would be $696,521.74.
At that revenue share ($696,521.74), the school budget would need to cut about $1.78 million from the level-services proposal.
Total cost increase including athletic transportation under the D-Bus contract is about $246,000 from last year, cited as roughly a quarter of the $2 million level-services increase.
Draft warrant article discussed with a specific dollar figure of $195,830, tied to a bid in hand for the project.
